title: Gai Pad Khing – Thai Ginger Chicken Stir-Fry

items: 300 g (10 oz) chicken breast or thigh, thinly sliced
100 g (3.5 oz) fresh ginger, julienned into fine matchsticks
150 g (5 oz) straw mushrooms or oyster mushrooms, halved
1 small red chili (prik chee faa), sliced thinly
1 handful wood ear mushrooms (optional, soaked if dried)
½ tsp dark soy sauce (for color)
2 tbsp neutral oil (rice bran, soybean, or canola)
White pepper, freshly ground, to finish

instructions.title: 1. Prepare Sauce
steps: In a small bowl, combine oyster sauce, light soy, fish sauce, dark soy, sugar, and chicken stock. Stir until sugar dissolves.

instructions.title: 2. Heat the Wok
steps: Place a well-seasoned wok over high heat until lightly smoking. Add oil and swirl to coat.

instructions.title: 3. Fry Aromatics
steps: Add garlic and stir-fry briefly (5–7 seconds) until fragrant, not browned. Immediately add chicken slices. Stir-fry until chicken is about 70% cooked.

instructions.title: 4. Add Vegetables
steps: Toss in onion, mushrooms, and half the ginger. Stir-fry quickly, keeping wok heat high for wok hei (charred aroma).

instructions.title: 5. Sauce It
steps: Add the premixed sauce. Toss everything together until chicken is fully cooked and sauce lightly coats ingredients.

instructions.title: 6. Finish with Fresh Ginger & Onion Greens
steps: Add the remaining ginger and spring onions. Toss briefly (10–15 seconds) to keep them crisp and aromatic.

instructions.title: 7. Plate & Serve
steps: Transfer immediately to a hot plate. Sprinkle with white pepper before serving.

tips: Knife Work: Cut ginger into fine, uniform matchsticks — not chunks — for a refined texture.
Layering Ginger: Cook half early for mellow warmth, add half at the end for fresh bite.
High Heat: True Thai wok technique relies on fast, high-heat cooking — avoid overcrowding.
Protein Tenderness: For extra succulence, marinate chicken with ½ tsp cornstarch and a dash of light soy for 10 minutes before cooking.
Balance: Taste the sauce before cooking; adjust fish sauce (saltiness) and sugar (balance).
